title: Doubt and possibility: es posible que, no es seguro que, quizás

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the subjunctive after doubt and probability: *dudo que* and *quizás* from B1 Unit 13. History is full of things nobody can prove, so these expressions are very useful: *Es posible que las epidemias sean la causa principal.*

items.spanish: Es posible que las epidemias sean la causa principal.
items.english: It is possible that the epidemics are the main cause.

items.spanish: No es seguro que podamos conocer la cifra exacta.
items.english: It is not certain that we can know the exact figure.

items.spanish: Quizás las causas actúen juntas en cada región.
items.english: Perhaps the causes act together in each region.

items.spanish: Los historiadores dudan que exista una sola explicación.
items.english: Historians doubt that there is a single explanation.

sections.content: Doubt and possibility take the subjunctive (*sean*, *podamos*, *actúen*, *exista*). Certainty takes the indicative: *No hay duda de que el mundo cambió*. *Quizás* can take the indicative when you are fairly sure, but the subjunctive shows real doubt.
